name: cloud-superapp
description: Diego's Cloud SuperApp — modularized monolith Android app. Single APK, gradle multi-module: app/ (launcher shell) + libs/{core,mail,cal,feed,net,ops,vault,chat}/ (independent feature modules). FairEmail-derived mail with JMAP, CalDAV/Radicale calendar, RSS, WireGuard tunnel, cloud ops dashboard, vault. Build via Nix devShell (gradle + AGP + Android SDK), one APK out.

android._doc_abi_filters: Native-library ABIs shipped in the APK. Defaults to arm64-v8a only because MapLibre Native (added in Push 2) ships ~15-18MB of .so per ABI; shipping all 4 default ABIs (arm64-v8a + armeabi-v7a + x86 + x86_64) inflates the APK from ~22MB to ~82MB. Every Samsung Galaxy from S8 (2017) onward + every modern Pixel is arm64, so this is safe for the user's device. To support 32-bit devices or x86 emulators, add 'armeabi-v7a' / 'x86_64' to this list and rebuild — no Kotlin / gradle edits needed.

signing._doc: ONE shared Cloud-constellation signing key for ALL Android apps (Cloud-Comms hub+forks, Cloud-Nav, Cloud-IDE, Cloud-SuperApp). The SAME key signs every app so cross-app signature-IPC + the in-app fleet updater never hit a signature mismatch. KEY LOCATION (raw credential + sops passwords live ONLY in the vault repo): A0_keys/providers/android/release.jks (OU=Cloud Constellation) + A0_keys/providers/android/signing.secrets.yaml. build.sh::_resolve_signing resolves $VAULT_DIR (default ~/git/cloud-vault) + sops-decrypts the passwords, exporting ANDROID_KEYSTORE_FILE/ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD/ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS/ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD which the gradle signingConfig reads. CI does the same via a vault checkout + the SOPS_AGE_KEY secret. THERE IS NO FALLBACK: if the key is unavailable the build FAILS LOUD telling you to use the one shared key — it never generates or substitutes a random/legacy key.

diagnostics._doc: On-device DevControlServer diagnostics → cloud sink + local download. Baked into BuildConfig.LOG_SINK_URL / LOG_SINK_STREAM by app/build.gradle. log_sink_url is our OpenObserve (the Loki-equivalent log store, openobserve on oci-apps) ingest, reached via the PUBLIC first-party analytics collector so NO credential is embedded in the public APK (the collector relays to openobserve server-side). '{stream}' in the url is replaced with log_sink_stream at runtime. EMPTY url = cloud push disabled (the 'Download logs' action still works fully); set it to the confirmed collector ingest path to enable one-tap 'Send logs to cloud'. Data-driven: change here, every app rebuild picks it up — never hardcode in Kotlin.

emulator._doc: build.sh emulator boots an arm64 AVD for FULL-FIDELITY testing of the arm64-v8a APK — the emulator emulates arm64 wholesale (TCG/software on this x86_64 host: slow but faithful), so NO libhoudini translation is involved (unlike the Waydroid path). The emulator binary + system image come from the Nix devShell (flake.nix composeAndroidPackages includeEmulator/includeSystemImages). system_image ABI+API MUST match flake.nix abiVersions/systemImageTypes/platformVersions. avd_name is created idempotently by build.sh from system_image; boot_args are passed verbatim to `emulator`.

toolchain._doc: Pinned for reproducibility — all derived in flake.nix. Bump here, rebuild devShell.
toolchain._doc_sdk_bump: compile_sdk bumped 34→35 to satisfy androidx.health.connect:connect-client:1.1.0-alpha10's AAR metadata constraint (it requires consumers to compile against Android 35+ for the new HC permission definitions wired to API 35 constants). AGP 8.5.2 maxes at compileSdk 34, so AGP bumped 8.5.2→8.7.3 (first stable AGP supporting compileSdk 35). Gradle 8.7→8.10.2 follows AGP 8.7's Gradle 8.9+ requirement. target_sdk stays at 34 — opting into Android 15 runtime behaviour is a separate concern from compiling against its APIs.
toolchain._doc_heliboard_bump: compile_sdk bumped 35→36 + the whole toolchain re-pinned to vendor HeliBoard main as libs:keyboard (self-contained keyboard provider). HeliBoard main pins AGP 8.13.2 / Kotlin 2.3.20 / Gradle 8.14 / compileSdk 36 (Android 16) / NDK 28.0.13004108, and uses the standalone Kotlin 2.0 Compose-compiler plugin (org.jetbrains.kotlin.plugin.compose) — so app + libs:wallet dropped composeOptions.kotlinCompilerExtensionVersion in favour of that plugin. nixpkgs channel bumped 24.11→25.05 because 24.11's androidenv/kotlin/gradle predate API 36 / Kotlin 2.3 / Gradle 8.14. target_sdk unchanged. See libs/keyboard/README.md.

upstreams._doc: Workspace tracking clones of upstream FOSS apps. Each lives at ../ea_<domain>-<project>/ (gitignored, see 0_git/src/gitignore ea_*-*/ rule). Refresh with `git -C ../ea_<x>-<y> pull`. Code is cherry-picked into libs/<domain>/ — NEVER built as a gradle subproject directly (they're top-level apps, not libraries).

kde-connect.license: GPL-2.0 (UPSTREAM REFERENCE ONLY — we do NOT vendor it)
kde-connect._doc_phase: CLEAN-ROOM, SELF-CONTAINED. libs/kde-connect is an ORIGINAL implementation of the KDE Connect LAN protocol written by us (NetworkPacket framing, mutual-TLS handshake with a self-signed device cert, protocol-v8 encrypted identity re-exchange, cert-pinned pairing, plugin registry: ping/clipboard/findmyphone/notification). The KDE repo above is consulted ONLY for the documented interop FACTS (port 1716; the TCP-dialer is the TLS server; pairing = trust-the-cert) — those are functional protocol requirements, not copyrightable expression. NONE of KDE's GPL-2.0 source is copied/vendored, so the app keeps its own license. Connects over wg0 by explicit wg_ip (auto-discovery can't cross WireGuard). Next: a foreground service hosting an inbound TCP server (1716-1764) so peers can also initiate, plus battery/share/mpris plugins.

firewall.license: Apache-2.0 (UPSTREAM REFERENCE ONLY — not vendored in v1)
firewall._doc_phase: CLEAN-ROOM, SELF-CONTAINED (v1). libs/firewall is ORIGINAL code: a minimal no-root per-app outbound firewall. A local VpnService captures traffic into a tun; ALLOWED apps are added via addDisallowedApplication() so they bypass the tunnel onto the real network, while BLOCKED apps fall into the tun and their packets are dropped (no forwarding loop) — zero root, zero native code. The RethinkDNS repo above (Apache-2.0, Kotlin) is consulted ONLY as the cherry-pick source for FUTURE complex tooling (DoH/DoT/DNSCrypt filtering, per-connection tracker, WireGuard proxying via its Go firestack engine). NO upstream source is copied/vendored in v1, so the app keeps its own license. Single VPN slot: while the firewall holds the device VPN slot, the libs:net WireGuard tunnel cannot run; unifying them is the first firestack cherry-pick. Sync the reference clone with: ./build.sh sync-firewall.

build._doc: Phase-2 firestack netstack build (`build.sh firestack`). VENDORED + hermetic like libwg-go: build.sh self-downloads the pinned Go (checksum-verified, cached under .cache/golang), then runs firestack's OWN `make <make_target>` (which go-installs gomobile@latest + gomobile init + gomobile bind) inside the Nix devShell for ANDROID_HOME + NDK. The built tun2socks.aar is copied to libs/firewall/firestack/<aar_out> — a flatDir aar folded INTO libs:firewall (NOT a standalone gradle module), consumed via `implementation(name:'firestack', ext:'aar')`. Java bindings land in package `java_pkg` (consumed by libs:firewall in Phase 3). gomobile@latest is upstream's pin choice — the one non-hermetic edge, tracked upstream.
build._doc_abi: gomobile bind defaults to ALL android ABIs (arm,arm64,x86,x86_64) — ~4× build time, blows the 30-min CI job. build.sh restricts it to the ONE ABI the SUPERAPP_VARIANT ships by overriding firestack's Makefile ANDROID23 var with a single -target. These flags MIRROR firestack Makefile's ANDROID23 (`-androidapi 23 -target=android -tags='android' -work`) minus the ABI; keep in sync on firestack bumps.

firestack._doc_phase: Phase 2 (build wiring). firestack is celzero/firestack (MPL-2.0, Go) — the gVisor-netstack + WireGuard-proxy engine behind RethinkDNS. We VENDOR + build it hermetically (user decision, matches the libs:net/libwg-go doctrine) rather than pulling the jitpack `com.github.celzero:firestack` Maven artifact. In Phase 3 the single firestack VpnService replaces BOTH FirewallVpnService (drain-engine) and GoBackend$VpnService (WireGuard); a per-connection `Bridge.Flow()` calls FirewallDecider direction-aware, and allowed flows route via the WG proxy — resolving the single-VPN-slot limit + enabling IN/OUT + the 'only under cloud VPN' condition. Nothing consumes the firestack aar yet (no consumer until Phase 3), so a plain `build.sh build`/`test` does NOT trigger the Go/gomobile build.

ops._doc_no_upstream: ops is a thin c3-api dashboard — no FOSS upstream to fork. Will be original code.

core._doc_no_upstream: core is shared infra (DB, theming, prefs, the updater) — original code.

modules._doc: Single source of truth for the Gradle module graph. settings.gradle iterates this list. Adding a new feature module = one entry here + mkdir + minimal build.gradle.

app.comment: Launcher / shell. Hosts navigation to each feature module.

libs:core.comment: Shared models, DB, theming, prefs, auth. No domain logic.

libs:updater.comment: In-app auto-updater. Periodic WorkManager check against ghcr.io via OCI HTTP API (same flow build.sh phone-install uses). If remote sha256 differs from current PackageInfo's, prompts user via PackageInstaller. All knobs in release.auto_update — no hardcoded URLs.

libs:appstore._doc: The Constellation store: fleet list, install/update actions, background pass. Split from the app so store, launcher and updater are separable - libs:updater is the engine, this is the storefront. UI, so it cannot go out-of-process like libs:net; the win is the boundary.

libs:mail.comment: Mail — FairEmail-derived, JMAP-extended. Source upstream: github.com/M66B/FairEmail (GPLv3). Tracking clone lives at ../ea_mail-fairmail/.

libs:feed._doc_not_linked: Declared so gradle can resolve the module tree, but the APP no longer depends on it: libs:feed ships as Cloud-Lib-Feed.apk and is reached through core's DataBackendClient (app rss/RemoteFeed.kt). This is the libs-are-the-backend split - the RSS/Atom fetcher lives in the engine APK, the app keeps only the UI.

libs:ops.comment: Cloud ops dashboard — c3-api, health checks, dagu trigger, container control.

libs:chat.comment: Chat / messaging. Likely integrates with mattermost-bots (chat.diegonmarcos.com) — could fork Mattermost-Mobile / SimpleX / Conversations later.

libs:health.comment: MyHealth — native Android Health Connect dashboard. Reads aggregated records (Steps, Distance, Floors, Elevation, HR, RHR, HRV, VO2max, BP, BloodGlucose, SpO2, Temperature, RespiratoryRate, Sleep+stages, Exercise, Weight/BodyFat/Lean/Bone/Water, Hydration, Nutrition, Cycle) via androidx.health.connect:connect-client. All of Garmin Connect / Google Fit / Samsung Health / Fitbit / Oura sync INTO Health Connect on-device — single SDK gets the union. LOCAL-ONLY: persists rollups + caches into HealthStore (libs:core, SharedPreferences). Zero network. No OAuth, no webhooks, no cloud ingester. Compose surface — pages declared in build.json::ui.sections[id=health].

modules._libs_browser_tombstone: libs:browser MOVED to ea_cloud-browser (constellation APK). Removed from app.depends_on and from this module list 2026-07. The Tools tile target is now extapp:cloud-browser. launchUri http/https now sends ACTION_VIEW to com.diegonmarcos.cloudbrowser instead of instantiating BrowserHostFragment.

libs:fin.comment: MyFin — personal finance dashboard. Beta renders from build.json::ui.myfin_mock (accounts, monthly stats, top expense categories, recent transactions, net worth) — all data-driven so the user can iterate the layout by editing JSON without rebuilding Kotlin. Real aggregator (Plaid / GoCardless / SaltEdge / manual OFX import) lands in a follow-up. MyFinDashboardFragment is the only surface for now; pages: dashboard.

libs:launcher-apptabs.comment: App Tabs — last-6 opened SuperApp entries (sections, pages, external apps) rendered as a 2-col GRID. Sister module to libs:browser; same card-grid UX, different content (sealed Entry: SectionEntry | PageEntry | ExternalAppEntry). AppTabPrefs is SharedPreferences-backed ('app_tabs' file, strict LRU cap=6). Producers call AppTabPrefs.recordSection / recordPage / recordExternalApp on every successful navigation; the GRID re-renders on onResume so flipping back to Tabs always shows the freshest LRU. AppTabsHost is the callback interface MainActivity implements to handle card-tap re-navigation without libs:launcher-apptabs reaching back into app/.

libs:kde-connect.comment: KDE Connect (Configs > KDE page). FULLY SELF-CONTAINED, CLEAN-ROOM — our own implementation of the KDE Connect LAN protocol, no org.kde.kdeconnect_tp dependency and NO KDE GPL source vendored. Pipeline: dial <wg_ip>:1716 over wg0 → write identity (plaintext) → mutual-TLS handshake AS the TLS server (BouncyCastle self-signed device cert; the dialer is the TLS server per the protocol) → re-exchange identity encrypted (v8) → cert-pinned pairing (KdeTrustStore) → NetworkPacket plugins (ping/clipboard/findmyphone/notification). Data-driven from ui.kde_connect (self_name + devices[].wg_ip); nothing hardcodes an IP. BouncyCastle (bcpkix/bcprov jdk15to18) is the only added dep, for cert generation. Next phase: foreground service + inbound TCP server so peers can initiate too.

libs:shizuku-adb-debug-tools.comment: Shizuku ADB debug tools — makes the SuperApp a SELF-CONTAINED 'adb shell' surface. A Shizuku UserService (IShellService.aidl + ShellUserService) runs in SHELL context (uid 2000) when Shizuku is running + granted, so it executes arbitrary `dumpsys` / `getprop` / `cat /sys/...` that the app's own uid + the SELinux-hardened proc/sys path can't reach (One UI 7+/Pixel A15+ block /sys/class/power_supply/*). ShizukuAdb is the binder facade (bindBlocking + exec + grantDump self-grant of android.permission.DUMP via `pm grant`). AdbDiagnostics runs DATA-DRIVEN command bundles declared in build.json::shizuku_diagnostics.bundles[] (charger/usb/battery/thermal/pd) and returns them as JSON. Exposed over the loopback DevControlServer at /api/adb/* (token-gated). This is the path that finally surfaces the USB-PD/PPS negotiation needed to debug 'why is the charger at 3W not 35W'.

libs:firewall.comment: No-root per-app outbound firewall. v2 = data-driven conditional per-app rules (FirewallRules/FirewallDecider/FirewallConditions, presets in assets/firewall_presets.json); interim drain-engine (FirewallVpnService). Phase 3 will consume the firestack netstack aar (flatDir libs/firewall/firestack/, `implementation(name:'firestack', ext:'aar')`) to run WG + per-app filtering + IN/OUT in one VpnService. Surfaced in About under Battery (info rows + 'Firewall Details' → FirewallDialog master switch + per-app preset picker).

libs:battery.comment: Battery/energy engine + its dialogs, extracted from app so it sits as a sibling of libs:firewall. Tier-1 (no-root): BatteryManager/sysfs correlation. Tier-2 (privileged): ShizukuEnergy reads `dumpsys batterystats` via the Shizuku user-service (IUserService/ShizukuUserService) now consolidated into libs:shizuku-adb-debug-tools — hence the lib→lib dep (not lib→app). Consumed by app/devcontrol (the About UI). Also the 'battery-manager' for per-app energy ranking (EnergyWatchdog.perAppEstimate) feeding the Phone 'Top Battery' smart folder.

libs:datamanager.comment: The 'data-manager' — pure per-app DATA providers, no UI. AppUsageProvider (UsageStatsManager: recency / active-window / launch-count) + AppNetworkProvider (NetworkStatsManager: per-app bytes), both gated on the PACKAGE_USAGE_STATS special-access already granted for the Battery & Usage screen. Sibling to libs:battery (the 'battery-manager', per-app energy). Providers return ranked package-name lists; app/apps maps them onto the launchable-app set for the Phone smart folders (Recent / Active 48h / Most Opened / Most Network) and the Suite/Phone 'Active Apps' section. Every query runCatching→empty so a missing grant just hides the folder.

libs:launcher-onehand.comment: One-Hand edge-gesture overlay (Samsung One Hand Operation+ style). A foreground EdgeOverlayService draws a thin near-invisible handle on the configured screen edge (WindowManager TYPE_APPLICATION_OVERLAY) and turns swipes into global actions (Back/Home/Recents/Notifications/QuickSettings) performed by OneHandAccessibilityService. Two user-granted special perms (SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW + Accessibility) — OneHandController does the deep-linking + start/stop; app/ (Configs/Onehand) is just the toggle. Fully data-driven from build.json::onehand (edge, handle size, gesture→action map baked to BuildConfig.ONEHAND_CONFIG_B64). PURE SwipeClassifier is JVM-tested. Home also has THREE stars atop this module: Sirius (SiriusStar, full circular-menu), Canopus (CanopusStar, arc-menu over Configs), and Centauri (CentaurusStar, SAME arc-menu, content = last 9 recently-opened Android apps via libs:datamanager's AppUsageProvider). ALL THREE star widget classes now live HERE (moved from app/launcher on request — 'ALL STARS in one-hand'), because ArcMenu/CircularMenu already define the app-agnostic Host boundary. Centauri needs no app callback at all (recent-apps + app icons + launch are pure platform APIs), so it takes no Host. Sirius/Canopus's CONTENT is still app-specific (Sections/SectionPages/CircularMenuTree), so THOSE classes take a Host (+ a twinkleEnabled callback for Sirius) injected from MainActivity, which builds it from its own app-side classes — the star mechanics (glyph, size, touch-forwarding, position, visibility) are generic and lib-side; only the content adapters stay in MainActivity.

libs:launcher-zoomies.comment: Zoomies pets — the animated status-bar companion. PetStrengthView (an AppCompatImageView) plays a per-tool animal whose gait (idle→walk→walk_fast→run) tracks the tool's strength, decoded from the vendored zoomies GIFs at assets/zoomies/<animal>/<variant>_<gait>.gif (CC BY-ND, used unmodified). Pure view module: no build.json config, no inter-lib deps — only androidx.appcompat. Consumed by app/launcher (LauncherStatusStripView instantiates one PetStrengthView per tool).

onehand._doc: One-Hand edge-gesture config for libs:launcher-onehand (One Hand Operation+ style), baked into BuildConfig.ONEHAND_CONFIG_B64 by libs/launcher-onehand/build.gradle and decoded by OneHandConfig. `handles[]` = one gesture pad per screen edge. Each handle: edge (left|right|bottom), position_pct (center offset along the edge), length_pct (pad length), thickness_dp (pad width), transparency (0=invisible..100=solid debug tint), edge_inset_dp (how far INSIDE the border the pad sits, leaving the very edge free for Samsung/Termux system gestures), and a `gestures` map. You activate the pad anywhere along it, then the TILT of the inward swipe picks one of three sectors: `top`|`center`|`down` (center=straight inward). Bottom edge → `left`|`center`|`right`. Values are actions: none|back|home|recents|notifications|quick_settings|power_dialog|split_screen|lock_screen|screenshot|dismiss_shade|all_apps (API-gated ones no-op on old Android) OR `app:<package>` to launch an app. Remap anything with a one-line JSON edit or in the in-app editor — never a Kotlin change (Pillar: DATA-DRIVEN).

circular_menu._doc: Sirius-star radial pie — the libs:launcher-onehand 'circular-menu', sibling to the edge-menu. Tapping the home star opens a ring of these nodes; a center arrow follows the finger, the pointed node highlights, and dragging past its ring DESCENDS into that node's children (which recenter and fan out again); releasing on a leaf navigates. Descent is RECURSIVE and arbitrary-depth: a node's `section` is its childKey — the app injects navigate(target) + iconBitmap(name) + childrenOf(key) (see app CircularMenuTree) so the lib stays app-agnostic and the tree mirrors the live sections. Example: Suite → {Cloud, Phone} → (Phone) {Home, More}; Comms/Infos → {Apps, Admin}; Labs/Configs → their pages. A node with `section:null` (Home Apps) is terminal. Star + nodes are data-driven — remap with a one-line edit, never Kotlin.

defaults._doc_gesture_inset: The handle is inset from the very border for TWO reasons on Samsung: (1) CURVED-EDGE display — the border pixels are on the curve, where touch is unreliable (edge/palm rejection) + reserved by the system, so a handle AT the edge never activates. (2) GESTURE-nav back-swipe fires from the edge and races our press. Both are dodged by placing the handle on the FLAT glass past the curve. edge_inset_dp (26) applies always (covers the curve); edge_inset_gesture_dp (30) is used in gesture-nav (curve + a bit more to clear the back-gesture strip), detected via config_navBarInteractionMode. Flat-screen devices can lower edge_inset_dp toward 0.
defaults._doc_geometry: BOUNDED band, not full-height. length_dp=180 (>0 overrides length_pct) keeps the touch zone a ~180dp band at position_pct down the edge. Two reasons it must be bounded: (1) our handle CONSUMES touches in its area (a touchable overlay can't pass them through), so a full-height strip creates a dead vertical band down the whole edge that blocks the app underneath (e.g. Bitwarden buttons near the edge stop responding). A short band frees the rest of the edge. (2) systemGestureExclusionRects is OS-capped at 200dp/edge, so ≤180dp is FULLY excluded → reliable. Invisible (transparency 0); it lives at a consistent thumb-zone position.

onehand._doc_apps: App vocabulary offered in the per-swipe action picker (OneHandFragment). Each entry launches its package via getLaunchIntentForPackage; a package the phone doesn't have is silently skipped at fire time. Add an app = one entry — no Kotlin change.
onehand._doc_radial: Two-finger radial menu (libs:launcher-onehand, OBSERVE-ONLY via the accessibility service's onMotionEvent — needs Android 14+). Hold TWO fingers anywhere ~still for two_finger_hold_ms → a ring of icons opens at that point; release to one finger and move it to the icon (arrow follows), lift to fire. Because it only observes touches, the app underneath also sees the fingers (may pinch) — that's the cost of not intercepting. items[] are actions: `app:<pkg>` or a global action id (back|home|recents|notifications|quick_settings|...). radius_dp = ring radius; slop_dp = how far the 2-finger centroid may drift before the hold cancels.

radial._doc_security: enabled=false by DEFAULT on purpose: the radial menu works by OBSERVING ALL touches system-wide (FLAG_SEND_MOTION_EVENTS), which is a genuine privacy/security capability — it can see taps anywhere, including over a password manager. Turn it on ONLY as a conscious opt-in. While disabled, the service never requests motion-event observation at all.

onehand._doc_home_swipes: Configurable home-screen swipe actions. swipe_up fires when the user flings upward while on the Home section (default opens the Home Apps drawer). swipe_left/swipe_right replace the circular walk-list step. Values: open_home_apps | open_last_superapp_page | open_last_android_app | walk_step_next | walk_step_prev.

shizuku_diagnostics._doc: Data-driven catalog of shell-domain diagnostic bundles run by libs:shizuku-adb-debug-tools. Two execution channels share this catalog (ladder, first ready wins): (1) local_server — OUR OWN app_process server (AdbShellServer) started once per boot via the adb one-liner from /api/adb/server-command; it runs in the SHELL SELinux domain (uid 2000) so dumpsys/usb/sysfs that untrusted_app is denied all work. NO third-party app. (2) Shizuku UserService — optional fallback when its app happens to be running. The lib's build.gradle base64-encodes bundles[] into BuildConfig.ADB_DIAG_BUNDLES_B64; AdbDiagnostics decodes + runs the chosen bundle, returning {bundle,label,channel,ok,results:[{id,cmd,out}]}. Adding a diagnostic = one entry here, no Kotlin edit (Pillar: DATA-DRIVEN). READ-ONLY diagnostics only — never a write/mutation.

local_server._doc: OUR app_process shell-domain server. Started by `adb shell CLASSPATH=<apk> app_process /system/bin <class> <token> <port>` (the /api/adb/server-command one-liner, run once per boot via wireless debugging). Loopback + per-boot random token. This is the self-contained replacement for the Shizuku app.

commands.cmd: for d in /sys/class/power_supply/*; do echo "== ${d##*/} =="; for f in type online present status charge_type usb_type voltage_now current_now current_max voltage_max input_current_limit constant_charge_current_max power_now temp; do v=$(cat "$d/$f" 2>/dev/null) && echo "$f=$v"; done; done
for d in /sys/class/typec/port*; do echo "== ${d##*/} =="; for f in power_role data_role vconn_source power_operation_mode; do v=$(cat "$d/$f" 2>/dev/null) && echo "$f=$v"; done; done
for f in /sys/class/android_usb/android0/state /sys/class/udc/*/state; do echo "$f=$(cat $f 2>/dev/null)"; done
for z in /sys/class/thermal/thermal_zone*; do t=$(cat "$z/type" 2>/dev/null); v=$(cat "$z/temp" 2>/dev/null); echo "$t=$v"; done
for d in /sys/class/typec/*; do echo "== $d =="; grep -sr . "$d" 2>/dev/null | sed 's#/sys/class/typec/##'; done

samsung_sfc._doc: Data-driven inputs for the SfcVerdict parser (libs:shizuku-adb-debug-tools/SfcVerdict.kt), baked into BuildConfig.SFC_CONFIG_B64 by this module's build.gradle. The parser is PURE / JVM-testable and reads NO hardcoded device data — the model->max-watts ceiling map lives here so a new Galaxy model is a one-line JSON edit, never a Kotlin change. `device_caps` is keyed by model-number PREFIX (parser matches the longest startsWith of `ro.product.model`); value = the device's MAXIMUM wired watts (a higher-rated cable/charger cannot exceed it). `high_voltage_mv_threshold` = the dumpsys mcv / Max-charging-voltage (mV) at/above which a high-voltage fast-charge contract is considered engaged (9V = 9000). `full_level_pct` = SOC at/above which fast charge tapers, so a 'not negotiating' verdict is expected, not a fault.

status_pets._doc: Status-bar Line 0 animated pets (vendored from github.com/KartikLabhshetwar/zoomies, sprites CC BY-ND 4.0 — used UNMODIFIED + credited). Each Line-1 tool gets a FIXED animal above it; the tool's strength maps to a gait level 0..3 = idle/walk/walk_fast/run (the animal stays, the gait speeds up). Fully data-driven: sync-zoomies vendors exactly the animal/variant GIFs referenced here; app/build.gradle bakes this block to BuildConfig.STATUS_PETS_B64; LauncherStatusStripView renders + drives it.

voice._doc: Offline voice-input (Vosk) model registry for libs:voice, behind the keyboard VOICE toolbar key. libs/voice/build.gradle bakes this into BuildConfig.VOICE_MODELS_JSON + VOICE_DEFAULT_LANGUAGE; VoiceModelManager downloads the model for the active keyboard language lazily on first use, unzips to filesDir/vosk/<dir>, then Vosk runs fully offline (no Google/system speech IME). Add a language = one entry. Small models keep each download ~40-50MB.

keyboard_dicts._doc: Bundled keyboard dictionaries → libs/keyboard/src/main/assets/dicts/ (HeliBoard's DictionaryInfoUtils.ASSETS_DICTIONARY_FOLDER). HeliBoard's verbatim mirror already ships main_<locale>.dict for these locales (word suggestions); sync-keyboard-dicts ADDS the matching emoji_<locale>.dict (emoji search) from codeberg.org/Helium314/aosp-dictionaries (GPL-3.0) so each supported language has FULL features. Additive copy (no --delete) so it composes with the HeliBoard mirror; run AFTER sync-heliboard (which rsync --delete's the mirror and would drop these). Locales/types data-driven — add a locale or a type (with its repo dir) = one entry. NOTE: `locales` = which dicts are BUNDLED (broad, for any language the user adds); `default_languages` = which keyboard subtypes are ENABLED on first run (App.initVendoredKeyboard via SubtypeSettings.addEnabledSubtype) — distinct lists.

Deliberately NARROW: it never touches package identifiers (helium314.keyboard.* — the manifest resolves the IME service by that namespace), nor upstream attribution/credit/license/URL text (legally the upstream's credit). english_ime_name is handled separately as an app/ resource override. Special-access perms (battery whitelist, default launcher, usage stats), Health Connect perms, and System auto-granted perms are computed AT RUNTIME inside DevControlFragment — they don't need a JSON list because they're either single-flag toggles or PackageManager-introspected sets.

ui._doc_search_scopes: Scope chips of the top search sheet (SearchSheetFragment). DECOUPLED from home_apps_tabs (renaming a search scope must NOT rename the Home-Apps body tabs). Each scope: `id` (also the result-group key), `label` (chip text), `kind` (which index builder populates its hits). Kinds: `cloud_apps` = cloud sections + tiles + home actions (navigable destinations); `phone_apps` = installed launchable apps (LauncherApps); `cloud_configs` = every section sub-page (config/settings/about surfaces) + cached consolidated.json service entries (tap copies the value); `phone_configs` = installed Android Settings activities enumerated from the device Settings package(s) (exported, self-labelled activities; tap launches that Settings screen — same spirit as the native Settings search). All chips ON by default; tapping toggles inclusion. Reorder/rename here — no Kotlin edit.
ui._doc_swipe_walk: Horizontal swipe (left/right) walk-list — the CIRCULAR ordered list of navigation stops the bottom-nav swipe-cycle steps through. Replaces the old 'cycle the 4 bottom-nav sections' behaviour: now it also visits each section's sub-pages (mode tabs + Cloud/Phone tabs + the Home-Apps overlay). Each stop: `section` (id in ui.sections, or 'home' for the Home-Apps sheet) + ONE optional refinement — `mode` (apps|admin, for Tabbed sections Infos/Labs), `tab` (cloud|phone, for Suite's SuiteCloudPhoneTabsFragment), or `sheet` (cloud|phone, opens the Home-Apps AppDrawerSheet on that body tab). Left-swipe = next (down the list), right-swipe = previous; wraps at both ends. Reorder/add/remove stops here — no Kotlin edit. Consumed by MainActivity.walkStep / Sections.swipeWalk().
ui._doc_phone_grid_columns: Column count for the Phone tab's folder grid. Mirrors tile_columns (6) so the two tabs share the same density rhythm.
ui._doc_phone_folders: Folder taxonomy for the Phone tab — categorised by function (main purpose of the app), not by manufacturer. The `label` keeps the user's prefix sort markers verbatim (_#, _, -, .#, .a, .b, >) so the order reads identically to native One UI. `order` is the lexicographic sort key (two-digit blocks let new folders slot between existing ones). `match_keywords` are case-insensitive matches against the app's `packageName` and `label`. Five syntaxes (PhoneAppClassifier.matches): (1) `pkg:com.foo.bar` = exact packageName; (2) `pkg^com.foo.` = packageName.startsWith; (3) `lbl:Exact Label` = label exact; (4) `lbl~substring` = label contains (min 3 chars); (5) plain string = legacy substring on `pkg + label` (REQUIRES min length 4 to suppress catastrophic false-positives like `bb` matching `bbva` AND every package containing the letters `bb` anywhere). First matching folder wins, first matching keyword inside a folder wins. PREFER `pkg:` for known installed apps — it's the only form that can't false-match. TWO distinct sinks, different roles: (a) `_New Apps` (id=new_apps, order=98, empty keywords) is the AUTOMATIC sink — anything our keyword list doesn't know yet lands here, signal to the user that a new app needs triage / a new keyword / a new folder; (b) `_Misc` (id=misc, order=99) is the MANUAL sink — give it specific keywords to deliberately push hand-picked apps there. New Apps shrinks as keywords improve; Misc only grows when the user adds something to it on purpose. Manufacturer (Google / Samsung / non-Play-Store) is metadata for Smart Folders (see phone_smart_folders below) — NOT a primary grouping criterion.
ui._doc_phone_sections: Top-level section headers in the Home Apps/Phone tab. Folders are bucketed under a section by their label's first character: System (_), Services (-), Tools A (.), Tools B (>). Order = render order. Empty sections (every folder empty) silently skipped. Phone tab renders one subhead per non-empty section + the folder grid below.
ui._doc_phone_smart_folders: Smart Folders rendered at the BOTTOM of the Home Apps/Phone tab — dynamic filters over the same LauncherApps.getActivityList enumeration the page uses. Apps still belong to their topical folder above; Smart Folders are an orthogonal cross-cut view by manufacturer / install-source. Rule types: pkg_prefix (any pkg starts-with one of values); pkg_eq (any pkg equals one of values); install_source_in (the app's install-source-of-record — installingPackageName OR initiatingPackageName from PackageManager.getInstallSourceInfo — IS one of values; use this to bucket apps by the store/installer that owns their updates); install_source_not (install source NOT in values — legacy catch-all for 'anything outside the official stores'); recently_installed (ranking rule: newest firstInstallTime first, capped at `limit`); recent_used (ranking: most-recently-used first via UsageStatsManager.lastTimeUsed, capped at `limit`); active_since (ranking: apps used within the last `window_h` hours, most-recent first, optional `limit`); most_opened (ranking: launch count via MOVE_TO_FOREGROUND events over 7d, capped at `limit`); top_network (ranking: total bytes rx+tx via NetworkStatsManager over 7d, capped at `limit`); top_battery (ranking: estimated mAh via libs:battery EnergyWatchdog.perAppEstimate, capped at `limit`). The five usage/network/battery ranking rules read through libs:datamanager (usage+network) / libs:battery (energy) and ALL need the PACKAGE_USAGE_STATS usage-access grant — without it each degrades to an empty (hidden) folder. The install-source values are real installer package names — verified on-device via /api/phone/classify (which dumps installing/initiating/system per app): com.android.vending=Google Play, com.sec.android.app.samsungapps=Galaxy Store, com.uptodown=Uptodown, org.fdroid.fdroid=F-Droid, com.google.android.packageinstaller=manual sideload (raw APK, no store), com.epicgames.portal=Epic, com.facebook.system=Meta's own installer.

Every item has a `target`: `self` brings Cloud-SuperApp home; `app:<pkg>` launches that package (installing the `install_app` companion APK if absent); `section:<id>` / `action:<id>` / `page:<...>` bring Cloud-SuperApp forward and dispatch via its shortcut_action handler (onTileClicked). The COMPACT menu shows the first `compact_action_count` (3); the EXPANDED view shows ALL of them (up to 5) plus a now-playing album-art card. Targets: `torch` toggles the flashlight (CameraManager.setTorchMode, no camera perm); `calc` opens the device calculator (Intent CATEGORY_APP_CALCULATOR); `screensaver` starts ScreensaverService (full-black cover overlay — see ui.screensaver); `lock` locks the screen (ScreenLocker); `action:<id>` routes through Cloud-SuperApp. Add/replace/reorder = edit here.

contexts._doc: Cloud-Nav is a single forkless app, so it has NO child apps — `children` is empty and line 3 is omitted when it is foreground. This context exists only so the Cloud Nav hub on line 2 bolds (match via match_prefixes) when com.diegonmarcos.cloudnav is in the foreground.

ui._doc_kde_connect: KDE Connect config consumed by libs:kde-connect (Configs > KDE page). FULLY SELF-CONTAINED, ORIGINAL (clean-room) implementation of the KDE Connect LAN protocol — NO dependency on org.kde.kdeconnect_tp, NOT its GPL source. Auto-discovery (UDP broadcast / mDNS) does NOT cross WireGuard, so the client connects by explicit wg_ip instead: it dials <wg_ip>:discovery_port (1716) over wg0, writes its identity, runs the KDE Connect mutual-TLS handshake AS THE TLS SERVER (the protocol rule: the side that dials the TCP becomes the TLS server), re-exchanges identity encrypted (protocol v8), then pumps NetworkPackets through the plugin registry (ping/clipboard/findmyphone/notification). Pairing = remembering the peer's certificate; reconnects are cert-pinned. `self_name` is our advertised device name; `package` is retained only for the legacy 'open official app' affordance, never required. `devices[]` = the wg_ip targets we can reach (Surface Pro = mesh node 'laptop' = 10.0.0.5). Add a target = append a device with its wg_ip; nothing in Kotlin hardcodes an IP. The phone running the app advertises itself via self_name (this device = Samsung Galaxy S21 @ wg 10.0.0.9).

kde_connect._doc_plugins: Full KDE Connect plugin catalog, shown on the KDE page. `status`=active means the `packet` IS advertised in our identity capabilities (so the desktop shows the plugin for this device) and the per-plugin toggle controls it. Two flavours of active: (a) HANDLED — a real KdePluginRegistry plugin processes the packet (ping, clipboard, findmyphone, notification, battery, share, mpris, systemvolume, runcommand, contacts, connectivity_report, lockdevice, telephony, + the request-side aliases); (b) ADVERTISED-ONLY STUB — listed + advertised for visibility/testing but with NO Kotlin handler yet, so inbound packets are ignored until a handler lands (sms, mousepad, presenter, sftp, photo, remotekeyboard, bigscreen, virtualmonitor, screenconnector, presenter_remote, sftp_browse, sms_request). The KDE page colours handled (lavender) vs advertised-only (amber). `dir` from the phone's view: in=we receive, out=we send, both. Promote a stub to handled = add a plugin in KdePluginRegistry with its id.
kde_connect._doc_commands: RunCommandPlugin command list — the desktop can trigger these on the phone (kdeconnect.runcommand). `type`: app=launch package `value`; url=open `value` in the browser. Data-driven; add a row, the desktop sees it. No permission needed.

deploy.note: APK produced in dist/. Side-loadable via adb or shared via Filebrowser.

release._doc: Data-driven publish targets for the APK. build.sh oras-push + build.sh gh-release read this block; the GHA workflow (1_cicd/src/cicd/ship-cloud-superapp.yml) invokes those engine commands — no hardcoded registry/tag strings in the workflow.

artifact._doc: Path under dist/ to publish. The `debug` key is the daily-driver build (R8 shrink-only since 2026-08-21 - minifyEnabled true with -dontobfuscate, so names/line numbers and therefore real stacktraces survive while unreachable library code is dropped; debug keystore) — it is THE app for this stack, not a side-by-side dev variant. The `release` key exists for when a true Play-Store-style release lifecycle lands; the GHA workflow picks debug for main pushes.

release._doc_variants: Per-ABI build variants. The CI workflow runs one job per variant (matrix); the engine reads SUPERAPP_VARIANT to override the ABI filter (→ gradle env SUPERAPP_ABIS), the dist artifact name, the GHCR tag suffix, and the GitHub-release asset name. `arm64` is the DEFAULT — when SUPERAPP_VARIANT is unset the engine behaves exactly as before (arm64-v8a, Cloud-SuperApp.apk, ghcr :latest). `x86_64` adds a parallel artifact for Waydroid / desktop emulators, published to the SAME rolling `latest` GitHub release under a distinct filename, and to GHCR under tag suffix `-x86_64`. `supported_abis` drives the updater's ABI→tag map (AUTO_UPDATE_TAG_MAP, baked in libs/updater): a device resolves its update tag by the first Build.SUPPORTED_ABIS entry that matches — native ABIs precede libhoudini-translated ones, so an x86_64 Waydroid correctly pulls `latest-x86_64`. `update_tag` MUST equal `latest` + `ghcr_tag_suffix` so the updater and the publisher agree. Add an ABI = append a variant here; no Kotlin/gradle/workflow edits beyond the matrix list.

ghcr._doc: ORAS push as an OCI artifact (not a container — APK is a blob). One :latest tag plus per-commit sha + per-version tags. Image renamed from `superapp` to `cloud-superapp` — old package becomes orphan.

gh_release._doc: GitHub Release attachment. rolling_tag is the canonical mode now: one release named (default `latest`) the ship workflow overwrites on every main push, so the linktree Android download link stays stable. tag_pattern stays as legacy for immutable per-tag releases when invoked under a tag push context (rolling release still publishes alongside).

phone_install._doc: Targets for build.sh phone-install. Pulls APK from GHCR via curl+OCI HTTP API (no oras dep — works on aarch64 Termux without a Nix shell) and copies to a target dir an Android file manager can see. Override target_dir per environment via PHONE_TARGET env var; default suits Termux/nix-on-droid where ~/storage symlinks to /storage/emulated/0/.

auto_update._doc: In-app updater config — read at gradle eval time into BuildConfig, then used by libs:updater at runtime. Same registry/namespace/image as release.ghcr (the engine asserts consistency at build time).
auto_update._doc_interval: WorkManager periodic minimum is 15 min. 6h matches typical update cadence + spares battery / data.
auto_update._doc_unmetered: true → automatic auto-download+install only on unmetered (Wi-Fi). On a metered network (mobile data) an automatic run does NOT download; it shows the 'Update available — Update now / Later' prompt so the user consents before spending data. Manual 'Check for updates' and the prompt's 'Update now' force a download on any network.
auto_update._doc_install: Declared default for the runtime Auto-update toggle (Configs/About → Permissions, user-overridable via AutoUpdatePrefs). 'silent' → installer commits with USER_ACTION_NOT_REQUIRED (no install prompt) once the one-time 'Install unknown apps' grant is given; without the grant Android transparently falls back to a prompt. 'prompt' → always USER_ACTION_REQUIRED.
auto_update._doc_max_installs_per_pass: Most install sessions ONE unattended background pass may open. A background pass cannot show the system install dialog (Android 10+ blocks background activity starts), so each install it starts leaves a tap-to-install notification holding a PackageInstaller session until the user answers it. Unbounded, one pass over the 40-entry fleet opens 40 and the installer hits Android's 50-session cap - 'Too many active sessions for UID'. The remainder is picked up by the next pass. User-initiated 'Update all' is NOT capped: it runs in the foreground where the dialog appears and sessions resolve at once.
